issues.title: Local interpolation data cannot bound the global dG-star seminorm
issues.failure_explanation: The dG-star seminorm contains sums over every mesh element and interior face, while I_h^K φ is defined only on K and the right-hand side contains only the H^n(K) norm. A function's behavior on other elements is therefore uncontrolled, and the displayed object is undefined unless an unstated global extension is supplied.
issues.overall_effect: The global interpolation estimate used to control the acoustic defect and subsequent pressure and coupled-system errors is unavailable as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the malformed local display by the global estimate |φ−I_hφ|_{dG,*} ≲ h^{n−1}‖φ‖_{H^n(Ω)} for the required range 2 ≤ n ≤ q+1. Establish it by summing the elementwise interpolation estimates and applying the continuous trace inequality to the normal-trace term, then use it for the global pressure interpolation errors and their time derivatives in the defect estimate. This preserves every listed downstream rate and conclusion.
issues.why_classification: The old source defines the global interpolant immediately before the lemma, and the downstream proof clearly requires the corresponding global estimate. Nevertheless, a complete repair requires a short global summation and trace argument, not merely correction of a harmless glyph. That work is routine and source-supported and causes no loss of hypotheses, rate, or guarantee, so the issue is minor rather than moderate or serious.

issues.title: L2-in-time discrete sources do not justify classical semidiscrete solutions

failure_location.quote: $F$ is locally Lipschitz continuous and bounded in $\closedball$

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The semidiscrete wave--convection-diffusion problem consists of finding $(\ph,\uh) \in C^{2}([0,T];\Vhq) \times C^{1}([0,T];\Vhq)$

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition invokes Picard–Lindelöf after treating F as locally Lipschitz and bounded, but F also contains the time-dependent acoustic sources, which the old assumptions place only in L2. For example, with κ=0 and an L2 forcing that alternates on intervals accumulating at zero, the forcing can satisfy the stated O(h^q) accuracy while no C2 pressure can satisfy the finite-dimensional equation on any interval from zero. Likewise, a discontinuous concentration forcing generally gives only an absolutely continuous solution, not the claimed C1 solution.
issues.overall_effect: Local classical existence, the continuation argument, and the claimed C2-pressure/C1-concentration well-posedness chain are not established under the old data class.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require each discrete volume and boundary source to be continuous in time with values in its stated finite-dimensional space, while retaining the existing L2-in-time approximation bounds, and propagate that hypothesis to the acoustic and coupled well-posedness results. The resulting nonautonomous finite-dimensional vector field is continuous in time and locally Lipschitz in the state, so Picard–Lindelöf yields the claimed C2 pressure and C1 concentration; the continuation and energy-error arguments then remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: This is a contained repair that preserves the method, convergence rates, and classical-solution conclusions, so no global reconstruction is needed. It is not minor, however, because the old source expressly admitted arbitrary L2-in-time discrete loads, including natural discontinuous loads, and continuity excludes a substantial part of that input class. The restriction is limited and the resulting theorem remains recognizably comparable, which places the issue at moderate rather than serious severity.

issues.title: Acoustic first-order ODE omits the nonlinear coefficient
issues.failure_explanation: The product rule gives ((1+κp_h)q_h)_t=(1+κp_h)q_{h,t}+κ(q_h)^2. The old F instead subtracts π_h((q_h)^2). In particular, when κ=0 the original semidiscrete acoustic problem is linear, while the constructed ODE remains nonlinear, so Picard–Lindelöf for that ODE does not prove local existence for the stated problem.
issues.overall_effect: The local-existence proposition and hence the continuation and error-analysis chain are not proved for the stated acoustic problem for general κ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the definition of F, replace −π_h((q_h)^2) by −π_h(κ(q_h)^2). The local-Lipschitz argument and all subsequent continuation and error estimates require no other change for this issue.
issues.why_classification: The factor κ is uniquely forced by expanding ((1+κp_h)q_h)_t and by the κ=0 specialization of the stated semidiscrete problem. Inserting that omitted scalar is a transcriptional correction; it neither changes the intended equation nor requires a new inference, estimate, or construction.

issues.title: Upwind volume term uses the test function instead of the trial function
issues.failure_explanation: For the old definition, the volume terms in b(v;u,w)-b(v;u_h,w) cancel because both equal -∫w(v·∇_h w), whereas the displayed b(v;u-u_h,w) still contains that generally nonzero quadratic term. Thus the error equation used to prove the theorem does not follow. More basically, scaling w by a scalar produces a quadratic contribution in an equation whose other terms are linear in w, so the stated variational problem need not have a solution.
issues.overall_effect: The existence and concentration-error conclusions of the full-model theorem are not established for the semidiscrete problem as defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the volume term in the upwind definition to −∫_Ω φ_h(v·∇_h w_h), replacing the erroneous first factor w_h by the trial function φ_h. This restores the standard bilinear upwind form, its stated positivity identity, the subtraction formula, and the concentration energy estimate without changing the theorem.
issues.why_classification: The two-argument form, its flux terms, the cited standard upwind formulation, and the later boundedness and error calculations all uniquely force the trial function in this slot. The reasoning consistently uses that intended bilinear form rather than the literal quadratic-in-the-test expression, so the one-symbol substitution is transcriptional and entails no mathematical loss or proof repair.

issues.title: Concentration convergence estimate omits an initial-data condition
issues.failure_explanation: At t=0 the theorem's estimate requires \|u_0-u_{0,h}\|_{L2}^2 to be O(h^{2q}), but the semidiscrete problem permits any u_{0,h} in V_h and the theorem adds no relation to u_0. In the error splitting, e_h^u(0)=I_hu_0-u_{0,h}; integrating the energy inequality must retain this initial energy unless it is controlled or made zero.
issues.overall_effect: The stated concentration convergence rate is false for arbitrary discrete initial concentration data, although the existence assertion may still be considered separately.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the initial approximation condition ‖u_0−u_{0,h}‖_{L2(Ω)} ≲ h^q, with u_{0,h}=I_hu_0 as a sufficient special choice. Retain ‖I_hu_0−u_{0,h}‖_{L2(Ω)}^2 as the initial energy when integrating the concentration error inequality and absorb it into the O(h^{2q}) bound.
issues.why_classification: A convergence estimate uniform down to t=0 necessarily needs control of the discrete initial concentration, so this is a genuine missing premise rather than a typo. The required condition is the standard local initialization assumption for an a priori estimate and leaves the method, model, conclusion, and convergence rate unchanged; no new lemma or nontrivial proof architecture is required.
